ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl:
Let I_{n,j} denote the half-open interval [j/n,(j+1)/n). Define J_{n,j}:[0,1/n)→I_{n,j} by J_{n,j}(d)=j/n+d.

First, J_{n,j} is well-defined into I_{n,j}: if d∈[0,1/n), then 0≤d<1/n, so
j/n ≤ j/n+d < j/n+1/n = (j+1)/n.
Hence J_{n,j}(d)∈[j/n,(j+1)/n)=I_{n,j}.

Second, J_{n,j} is injective: if J_{n,j}(d_1)=J_{n,j}(d_2), then
j/n+d_1 = j/n+d_2,
so d_1=d_2.

Third, J_{n,j} is surjective onto I_{n,j}: given any x∈I_{n,j}, set d=x-j/n. Since x∈[j/n,(j+1)/n), we have 0≤x-j/n<1/n, so d∈[0,1/n). Then
J_{n,j}(d)=j/n+(x-j/n)=x.
Thus every x in I_{n,j} has a preimage.

Therefore J_{n,j} is a bijection from [0,1/n) onto I_{n,j}. Moreover, the inverse map is exactly x↦x-j/n, because for d∈[0,1/n),
(J_{n,j})^{-1}(J_{n,j}(d))=d,
and for x∈I_{n,j},
J_{n,j}((J_{n,j})^{-1}(x))=x.
So the inverse function is x↦x-j/n.
